newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips tumble before close on ringgit fall.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips tumble before close on ringgit fall.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares tumbled during the afternoon session after the ringgit broke the crucial 2.80 pscychological barrier against the U.S. dollar, said analysts and dealers.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 8.36 points, 0.91 percent, lower at 910.18. It had earlier peaked at 929.50 before the lunch break.
"It seems to be reacting to the ringgit's fall. There is a lot of negative reaction from Singapore," said a vice president of futures trading at a local brokerage house.
The ringgit dipped to 2.8250 before recovering to 2.7800 at 0908 GMT.
"The market is very, very nervous at the moment," said Tony Shue, vice president of dealing at Jupiter Securities.
The ringgit on Friday hit its lowest levels since the currency was first floated in 1973.
The fresh round of selling on the ringgit came mainly from foreign funds out of Singapore, said analysts.
Malaysia's Consumer Price Index for July grew by 2.1 percent from the same month in 1996, the Statistics Department said earlier.
Share prices had staged a strong technical rebound since Wednesday after several days of selling by foreign funds.
Market volume stood at 285 million shares, valued at 1.60 billion ringgit. Losers swamped gainers 451 to 179.
Among the hardest hit stocks were key blue-chips such as Tenaga, Telekom and Magnum, losing 20 cents each.
Sime Darby closed up five cents at 7.90 ringgit, but had earlier peaked at 7.95 ringgit.
Bucking the trend in the afternoon session was UMW, which held on to a 25 cent gain at 8.05 ringgit, after having peaked at 8.20 ringgit.
Analysts said the stock was trading at an average price-to-earnings ratio of six-times 1998 earnings, and based on its recent half-year earnings, was cheap.
"People have just realised that it is incredibly cheap at six-times 1998 earnings," said Chehan Perera, auto analyst at ABN Amro Hoare Govett in Kuala Lumpur.
The company recorded a 69 percent increase in net earnings for the six months to June 30, 1997, compared to the same period in 1996
On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot August contract fell 23 points to 895.5 with 1,580 lots traded. September futures shed 26 points to 896.0 with 23 lots traded.
